additions.reason: The concept of שָׁרֶשׁ (soul-root) is the central and sole conceptual anchor of Torah #238. The entire teaching explains why a third person instinctively sides with one of two disputants: because one disputant is sָמוּךְ לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ (closer to the third party's root) more than the other. The Torah does not equate שרש to any other concept via bechina language — it uses שרש as a given principle (a metaphysical postulate) rather than a bechina node. It is therefore not part of any bechina package for this Torah, but it is the dominant conceptual node of the entire teaching and should be flagged as a future candidate for a bechina edge if cross-Torah connections are identified.

additions.reason: The agreement (הסכמה) of the third party is the phenomenon the Torah explains. It is presented as the natural outcome (eitza) of closeness to the shoresh, not as a bechina equivalence to another concept. Not present in the dataset for Torah #238.
additions.source_quote: אֲזַי יַסְכִּים עִם אֶחָד יוֹתֵר מֵעִם חֲבֵרוֹ

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: שָׁרֶשׁ (root/soul-root) — the central concept; the third party sides with one disputant because he is closer to his shoresh. Used as a causal principle, not a bechina equivalence. No bechina edge exists for this concept in Torah #238.
הַסְכָּמָה (agreement/accord) — the phenomenon explained by the Torah; result of shoresh-proximity. Causal, not bechina.
שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים מְחֻלָּקִים (two divided people) — the disputants in the scenario. Structural role, not bechina node.
הַשְּׁלִישִׁי (the third person) — the arbitrating third party whose shoresh proximity determines alignment. Structural role, not bechina node.
analysis_notes.note_on_torah_character: Torah #238 is one of the shortest and most structurally simple Torahs in Likutay Moharan. It is a pure aphorism: a single causal observation about human nature and the metaphysics of soul-roots (שָׁרֶשׁ). Unlike the elaborate multi-concept Torahs (e.g., Torah #1, #3), it contains no chain of bechina equivalences, no symbolic identifications, and no multi-stage argument. The word 'בחינת' does not appear anywhere in the text. The entire teaching is one causal claim: closeness-to-shoresh PRODUCES instinctive agreement. This is eitza (cause-effect), not bechina (shared nature). Therefore the bechina subgraph for Torah #238 is legitimately empty, and no packages can be proposed from connected components.
analysis_notes.recommendation: If future editorial work adds bechina edges for Torah #238, the most natural candidate would be cross-Torah edges connecting שָׁרֶשׁ to cognate concepts in other Torahs (e.g., Torahs that use שרש explicitly as a bechina node). Within Torah #238 itself, the aphoristic structure does not lend itself to bechina edge encoding.
